2026_352_transmittal_letter_for_fy27_pro.paragraph: Transmittal letter dated March 25, 2026 from Oakland Schools Superintendent Kenneth Gutman forwarding the proposed Oakland Schools FY 2026-27 budget to the boards of education of constituent districts, as required by Michigan School Code Section 380.624(2). Budgets for all Oakland Schools funds are enclosed for transparency, but constituent districts vote only on the General Fund budget. Oakland Schools projects a growth factor in its property tax revenues of 3.4%, and each constituent board must adopt a resolution of support or non-support not later than June 1, 2026.
2026_352_transmittal_letter_for_fy27_pro.page:
**What it is**
Cover letter, dated March 25, 2026, from Kenneth Gutman, Superintendent of Oakland Schools, addressed to "Dear Board of Education Designate," transmitting the proposed Oakland Schools budget for FY 2026-27 for constituent district review. Copies to District Superintendent and District Business Manager. Paginated as page ii of the budget document.

**Statutory basis**
Michigan School Code, Section 380.624(2) requires the proposed FY 2026-27 General Fund budget to be submitted to constituent district Boards of Education for review. Oakland Schools includes budgets for all of its funds for transparency, but only the General Fund budget is voted on by constituent districts and LEA Designates.

**Revenue outlook**
Oakland Schools is primarily funded by property tax dollars. A growth factor of 3.4% is projected in Oakland Schools' property tax revenues. Tax revenue projections are described as conservative compared with Oakland County taxable value increase projections, because actual taxable value figures are not available while the budget is prepared.

**Key projects and initiatives**
The Enterprise-Wide Executive Summary is cited for discussion of initiatives in the 2026-27 budget, including:

- Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy and Capacity Building
- Special Populations Continuum of Supports
- Social-Emotional Wellbeing and Mental Health Support
- Nanotechnology, Artificial Intelligence and Synthetic Biology (NAIS) Lab
- Oakland Schools Technical Campus Renovations
- Business Office Residency Program
- Human Resources Leadership Academy (HRLA)
- Essential Practices in Instruction to Capacity & Coherence (EPIC) Numeracy Project
- Literacy Essentials Oakland (LEO)

**Subsidies and personnel**
Oakland Schools provides over $1.4 million in subsidies for software and other instructional tools in Career and Technical Education and in curriculum and assessment; those subsidies are detailed in the budget document and exclude pass-through grant funds, other district allocations, and the cost of dedicated staff supporting student and HR/Finance software and applications. The budget includes step increases for eligible employees plus a 2.0% salary increase for all staff; all union salary changes, including step adjustments, remain subject to collective bargaining.

**PA-18 special education funding**

| Item | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Base PA-18 distribution increase to local districts | approximately $5.2 million, or 2.9% |
| Other LEA distributions (group homes, incarcerated youth reimbursement, special education startup, extraordinary expenditures, capital) | $2.5 million |
| Construction of an Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Center Program in Oxford | $5.0 million |
| Additional PA-18 funds distributed above base in FY 2025-26 | $5.8 million |

**Planning**
Oakland Schools uses a five-year forecast updated with each budget amendment, incorporating Oakland County Equalization projections for taxable values, and maintains a five-year capital plan updated annually for facility and equipment improvements.

**Calendar and process**
Submission to constituent districts for review by May 1. Presentation of the budget to the 28 local school district business managers at the Oakland County School Business Officials meeting on April 17, 2026. Oakland Schools Board of Education Designates Meeting on April 29 at 6:00 PM. Constituent board resolutions due to Oakland Schools on or before June 1, 2026. Truth in Budgeting hearing June 1, with the Oakland Schools Board considering the FY 2026-27 proposed budget documents for approval at its regular meeting that night. Questions directed to the Superintendent's office at 248.209.2424.
2026_352_transmittal_letter_for_fy27_pro.verbose:
Correspondence from Oakland Schools transmitting its proposed FY 2026-27 budget to constituent district boards of education. The letter is dated March 25, 2026, opens "Dear Board of Education Designate," and is signed by Kenneth Gutman, Superintendent, Oakland Schools, with copies to the District Superintendent and the District Business Manager. It appears as page ii of the budget document and was placed before the Troy School District Board of Education for its May 19, 2026 meeting.

STATUTORY REQUIREMENT AND SCOPE OF THE VOTE. The Oakland Schools Board of Education and the Superintendent invite constituent boards to review the enclosed proposed Oakland Schools budget for FY 2026-27. Per the Michigan School Code, Section 380.624(2), the proposed FY 2026-27 General Fund budget is to be submitted to constituent district Boards of Education for review. For transparency purposes, Oakland Schools has included the budgets for all of its funds in the enclosed document; however, it is only the General Fund budget upon which constituent districts vote. The letter repeats this point at the end, noting that while Oakland Schools provides all of its fund budgets to constituent districts for review, LEA Designates vote only on the General Fund budget.

PROPERTY TAX REVENUE ASSUMPTION. Oakland Schools is primarily funded by property tax dollars. The budget projects a growth factor in Oakland Schools' property tax revenues of 3.4%. The letter characterizes tax revenue projections as conservative compared to Oakland County taxable value increase projections, because actual taxable value figures are not available during preparation of the budget.

KEY PROJECTS AND INITIATIVES. Readers are referred to the Enterprise-Wide Executive Summary for discussion of key projects and initiatives contained in the 2026-27 budget, including but not limited to: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy and Capacity Building; Special Populations Continuum of Supports; Social-Emotional Wellbeing and Mental Health Support; the Nanotechnology, Artificial Intelligence and Synthetic Biology (NAIS) Lab; Oakland Schools Technical Campus Renovations; the Business Office Residency Program; the Human Resources Leadership Academy (HRLA); the Essential Practices in Instruction to Capacity & Coherence (EPIC) Numeracy Project; and Literacy Essentials Oakland (LEO).

SUBSIDIES. Under the heading Subsidies, the letter states that Oakland Schools provides over $1.4 million in subsidies for software and other instructional tools in the areas of Career and Technical Education and curriculum and assessment. The subsidies provided in the 2026-27 budget are detailed within the budget document and are exclusive of pass-through grant funds, other district allocations, and the cost of dedicated staff who support student and HR/Finance software and applications.

PERSONNEL COSTS. Step increases for those employees who are eligible are included in the 2026-27 budget, along with a 2.0% salary increase for all staff. All union salary changes, including step adjustments, are subject to collective bargaining.

PA-18 SPECIAL EDUCATION FUNDING. Oakland Schools receives property tax revenue for support of Special Education programs. The base distribution of PA-18 funding to local school districts is budgeted to increase approximately $5.2 million, or 2.9%. In addition, $2.5 million is budgeted for other LEA distributions covering group home expenditures, reimbursements to districts for educating incarcerated youth, special education program startup and extraordinary expenditures, and capital. The budget also contains $5.0 million for the construction of an Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Center Program in Oxford. In FY 2025-26, Oakland Schools distributed additional PA-18 funds totaling $5.8 million above the base distribution.

PLANNING FOR THE FUTURE. Oakland Schools states that it is dedicated to sound financial planning and to preparing for future economic uncertainties. It uses a five-year forecast that is updated with each budget amendment and that incorporates projections from Oakland County Equalization for taxable values. It also maintains a five-year capital plan, updated annually, to prepare for necessary improvements and upgrades to facilities and equipment. The Superintendent reiterates a commitment to increasing student achievement, using economies of scale to decrease operating costs for local districts, customizing and regionalizing programs and services to meet the diverse needs of constituent school districts, and assisting schools and districts in meeting state and federal mandates.

REVIEW AND APPROVAL TIMELINE. Per Section 380.624(2), the proposed FY 2026-27 General Fund budget is to be submitted to constituent districts' Boards of Education for review by May 1. Not later than June 1, the board of each constituent district shall adopt a resolution of support or non-support of the General Fund budget. A presentation of the budget to the 28 local school district business managers was scheduled to occur at their meeting of the Oakland County School Business Officials on April 17, 2026. The Oakland Schools Board of Education would then hold a Designates Meeting on April 29 at 6:00 PM, giving local board designates and district administration an opportunity to review the General Fund budget before submitting their board's resolution to Oakland Schools on or before June 1, 2026. The Oakland Schools Board of Education will hold a Truth in Budgeting hearing on June 1 and will consider the FY 2026-27 proposed budget documents for approval during its regular meeting that night.

CONTACT. Questions regarding the budget are to be directed to the Superintendent's office at 248.209.2424, with the letter promising prompt replies to all questions.

2026_353_2_e_tsd_budget_amendment_3_for_.paragraph: Troy School District Board of Education presentation for Amendment #3, June 2026, combining the truth-in-taxation public hearing, establishment of millage rates, final 2025-2026 budget amendments, and proposed 2026-2027 budgets for the General Fund, ancillary funds and special revenue funds. The 2026-2027 proposed General Fund shows revenue of $192,228,696, expenditures of $194,199,428 and an ending fund balance of $25,996,428, equal to 13.39%. The proposal assumes a blended FTE count of 11,869, down from the current 12,069, and sets a target of $12 million in General Fund expenditure reductions.

It presents 2025-2026 final amendments alongside 2026-2027 budget proposals.

**Taxable values**
Homestead is defined as a taxpayer's primary residence or non-commercial agriculture; non-homestead as business or rental properties, secondary homes, vacation homes, and commercial agriculture; total taxable value is the combination, with increases capped at the lesser of the rate of inflation or 5%.

**Assumptions, priorities and challenges**

Challenges listed are enrollment, lack of urgency in Lansing, the revenue landscape, rising expenditures, salary and benefits, retirement costs, and special education. Reduction targets cite maintaining instructional priorities, structural balance and a 15% fund balance target.

2026_353_2_e_tsd_budget_amendment_3_for_.verbose:
Board of Education budget presentation for the Troy School District titled Amendment #3, June 2026. The deck frames a public hearing covering truth in taxation, establishment of millage rates, budget adjustments and budget assumptions, then walks through the General Fund, the ancillary funds (2023 Capital Projects, Debt Funds, Building Site & Sinking, Capital Maintenance) and the special revenue funds (Food Service, Troy Career Center, Troy Preschool, School and Student Activities), presenting 2025-2026 final amendments together with 2026-2027 budget proposals.

TAXABLE VALUE DEFINITIONS. Homestead property is a taxpayer's primary residence or non-commercial agriculture. Non-homestead property covers business or rental properties, secondary homes, vacation homes and commercial agriculture. Total taxable value is the combination of homestead and non-homestead values, and taxable value increases are capped at the lesser of the rate of inflation or 5%.

TAXABLE VALUES BY YEAR. For 2025 the presentation reports homestead taxable value of 3,657,042,480, non-homestead taxable value of 1,953,185,000, and total taxable value of 5,610,227,480. For 2026 it reports homestead taxable value of 3,800,792,510, non-homestead taxable value of 2,064,220,210, and total taxable value of 5,865,012,720.

MILLAGE STRUCTURE. The State Education Tax is 6 mills levied on homestead and non-homestead properties, required by the State of Michigan toward the foundation allowance. The operating millage is 18 mills levied on non-homestead properties by the school district. The Hold Harmless millage rate is based on enrollment, taxable values and the foundation allowance, is calculated annually, and is levied on homestead properties; FY25 was 2.7294 mills. Sinking Fund and Debt Fund millages are levied by the school district on both homestead and non-homestead properties; FY25 was 0.9606 mills for the Sinking Fund and 6.1000 mills for the Debt Funds. The Headlee Amendment, approved by Michigan voters in 1978 as an amendment to the Michigan Constitution, automatically rolls back a millage rate so taxes do not increase more than the rate of inflation, and the district must annually calculate any applicable rollbacks to the operating millages and the sinking fund millage.

MILLAGE COMPARISONS. For homestead property across 2024-2025, 2025-2026 and 2026-2027: Debt 6.1000, 6.1000, 6.1000; State Education Tax 6.0000, 6.0000, 6.0000; Hold Harmless 2.7294, 2.5796, 2.4102; Sinking Fund 0.9606, 0.9540, 0.9472. For non-homestead property across the same three years: operating 18.0000, 18.0000, 18.0000; Debt 6.1000, 6.1000, 6.1000; State Education Tax 6.0000, 6.0000, 6.0000; Sinking Fund 0.9606, 0.9540, 0.9472. Total millage comparisons show homestead totals of 15.7900, 15.6336 and 15.4574 and non-homestead totals of 31.0606, 31.0540 and 31.0472 for 2024-2025, 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 respectively.

GENERAL FUND BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS, 2025-2026 AMENDMENT #3. Four adjustments are listed: categorical funding adjusted to reflect the anticipated final state aid status report; federal grant funding adjusted to reflect anticipated final allocations; ISD related funding sources adjusted to reflect anticipated final allocations; and purchased services, salaries and benefits budgets adjusted to reflect anticipated final expenditures.

GENERAL FUND ASSUMPTIONS, 2026-2027 PROPOSED BUDGET. The presentation uses the lowest proposed budget for each categorical and for the foundation allowance among the Governor, House and Senate proposals; assumes a blended FTE count of 11,869, a decrease from the current blended FTE count of 12,069; states that the lowest foundation allowance per pupil proposed and utilized is $250; and sets a target of $12 million of General Fund expenditure reductions.

BUDGET PRIORITIES. Securing known expenditure obligations through 2029, which the district says allows multi-year budget projections for staffing plans, better alignment as strategic planning begins, and labor stability and increased morale during challenging economic times. Data-driven alignment of student support services, including support for MTSS teams K-12, development and implementation support for a K-8 reading curriculum, and continued support for math implementation and student support. Reductions through attrition where feasible, a method used over the last three years to avoid layoffs through strategic use of fund balance; the deck notes that 95% of the budget is people with limited options available, that any RIF would be viewed through the lens of least impact on student achievement, and that a possible Employee Severance Plan will be reviewed.

BUDGETARY CHALLENGES AND REDUCTION TARGETS. Challenges listed are enrollment, lack of urgency in Lansing, the revenue landscape, rising expenditures, salary and benefits, retirement costs, and special education. Reduction targets are framed around maintaining instructional priorities, structural balance and a 15% fund balance target, with proposed targets of $12 million in reductions drawn from salaries and benefits, purchased services, departmental adjustments and discretionary spending. A Budget Reduction Rubric and Scoring slide is included. Proposed reductions identify areas for consideration including positions not directly connected to the classroom, maximizing adult-to-student ratios and contract allowances, and implementing a realignment of administrative and support staffing to better match current needs and resources.

GENERAL FUND FIGURES. 2026_354_2026_spring_bylaws_full_documen.paragraph: Complete bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association (OCSBA) presented in full with the spring 2026 proposed amendments shown in place, flagged as affecting pages 4, 8 and 9. The document records adoption by the Board of Directors on 11/15/2017, by the General Membership on 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018, and amendments approved by Member School Districts on 9/16/2020, 9/10/2021, 3/3/2023 and 6/6/2025. Sixteen articles plus Appendix 1 govern membership, dues, elections, officers, committees, finances, indemnification and amendment, with resolutions becoming Association policy only when approved by at least nineteen Member School Districts.
2026_354_2026_spring_bylaws_full_documen.page:
**What it is**
The full text of the OCSBA Bylaws with the May 2026 proposed amendments incorporated, marked "PROPOSED CHANGES PAGES 4, 8 AND 9." Adoption history: Board of Directors 11/15/2017; General Membership 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018; amendments approved by Member School Districts 9/16/2020, 9/10/2021, 3/3/2023 and 6/6/2025.

**Articles I-IV: offices, purpose, membership, dues**
Principal office at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland, plus a continuously maintained registered office and agent. Purposes (a)-(h) include advancing public education quality in Oakland County, informing board members, sponsoring programs in partnership with Oakland Schools, and advocating for county, state and national legislation. Membership is open to any publicly elected Oakland County board of education member or elected Oakland ISD board member in good standing with MASB. Each Member has one vote, except that each Member School District has one vote on resolutions (Article IX) and bylaw amendments (Article XVI); electronic voting is limited to the Board for emergency business, reaffirmed at its next meeting. Financing comes from an annual MASB grant to CASBA members, ISD dues not to exceed that grant, and contributions and gifts.

**Articles V-VII: meetings and the Board of Directors**
An annual meeting plus at least three additional regular membership meetings each year; the annual meeting is the first regular meeting after July 1. Special member meetings require 30 days' notice; written notice runs not less than ten nor more than fifty days before a meeting. Member quorum is at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of Member School Districts. The Board has an odd number of Directors, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9, serving three-year terms; the ISD, which pays dues directly, may appoint one Trustee to a 3-year term. An Election Committee of the three most recently elected Directors is convened by May 1, with election at the June meeting and no floor nominations. Missing three consecutive Board meetings constitutes resignation absent an excused absence requested in writing within thirty days. Board special-meeting notice is at least two days; Board proceedings are confidential.

**Articles VIII-IX: officers and committees**
Officers are a President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer elected from the sitting Board; the Secretary role may be split into Corresponding and Recording Secretary. Committee quorum is twenty-five (25%) percent of appointed representatives, alternates counting only when the primary is absent. Where an elected committee chair is not a Board member, the Association Board appoints one of its Directors as Vice-Chair. The Government Relations Committee meets at least 6 times per year and elects its chair at the first meeting after January 31; the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee meets at least once per year. Voting windows run at least forty (40) calendar days, and resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts become the official position of the Association.

**Articles X-XVI and Appendix 1**
Dissolution follows Article VIII of the Articles of Incorporation, with no inurement under Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. Expenditures over $2,500 require Board approval plus President and Treasurer signatures; expenditures up to $2,500 may be approved by either. The Treasurer presents a budget for the July 1-June 30 fiscal year no later than the June Board meeting and year-end revenue and expense reports no later than August 30. An external audit occurs only if required by law or a third party, and the Board may contract Administrative and Financial Services with Oakland Schools. Article XII sets out indemnification under the Michigan Nonprofit Association Act. Bylaws are amended by Member School District vote on a written ballot with at least a forty-day voting period. Appendix 1, adopted September 16, 2020, defines cause for removal around the duties of care, loyalty and obedience.
2026_354_2026_spring_bylaws_full_documen.verbose:
Full bylaws text of the Oakland County School Boards Association ("the Association," OCSBA), circulated in spring 2026 showing the proposed amendments in place. A cover page records adoption by the Board of Directors on 11/15/2017, adoption by the General Membership on 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018, and amendments approved by Member School Districts on 9/16/2020, 9/10/2021, 3/3/2023 and 6/6/2025, and states that the PROPOSED CHANGES can be found on PAGES 4, 8 AND 9 of the bylaws. The document runs 18 pages including Appendix 1.

ARTICLE I - OFFICES. Section 1 places the principal office of the Association in the State of Michigan at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland, with authority to maintain other offices inside or outside Michigan as the Board of Directors determines. Section 2 requires a continuously maintained registered office and a registered agent whose office is identical with the registered office; the registered office need not be identical with the principal office and its address may be changed by the Board.

ARTICLE II - PURPOSE. Eight stated purposes: (a) advance the quality of public education in Oakland County through cooperative efforts of locally elected boards of education; (b) promote high standards in educational programs and services for all students; (c) make information on educational issues available to school board members; (d) conduct and sponsor meetings and programs about education in partnership with Oakland Schools; (e) promote public understanding of the role of school boards and the need for citizen involvement; (f) enhance cooperation and communication among Oakland County boards of education; (g) present a strong force representing school board views to political representatives; and (h) advocate for county, state and national legislation and governance supporting public education by locally elected boards.

ARTICLE III - MEMBERSHIP. Section 1 organizes the Association on a membership basis; any publicly elected Board of Education member of a school district located in Oakland County, or any elected Oakland ISD Board of Education member (collectively "Member School Districts"), that is also a member in good standing in the Michigan Association of School Boards ("MASB"), is an eligible general member. Section 2 gives each Member one vote on each matter submitted to a vote, with all voting done in person, except that each Member School District has one vote on resolutions (Article IX) and on amendments to the Bylaws (Article XVI); district votes are recorded upon receipt of the completed resolution or ballot indicating the vote of the district's Trustees, must be received before the stated deadline, and results must be provided to all Member Districts not later than the next general membership meeting. Section 3 grants electronic voting rights to the Board of Directors only for emergency business, with all electronic votes reaffirmed at the next Board meeting. Section 4 makes membership non-transferable and non-assignable.

ARTICLE IV - DUES. The Association is financed by an annual MASB grant to its County Area School Boards Association (CASBA) members, by Intermediate School District membership dues in an amount not to exceed the MASB CASBA grant, and by contributions and gifts accepted by the Association.

ARTICLE V - MEETING OF MEMBERS. There shall be an annual meeting and not less than three additional regular membership meetings each year for appointing the Board of Directors and other business; the annual meeting is the first regular meeting after July 1, with date, time and place set by the Board. Special meetings may be called by voice or email by the President or by two or more Board members with 30 days' notice. Absent a designation, meetings are held at the registered office; a meeting held with all Members present and consenting is valid without call or notice. Written notice stating place, day and hour is delivered personally or by email by the Secretary not less than ten nor more than fifty days before the meeting, with purposes stated for special meetings; mailed notice is deemed delivered when deposited in the United States mail with postage prepaid. Action may be taken without a meeting by written consent signed by all Members entitled to vote. Quorum is the presence of at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of the Member School Districts; without a quorum a majority of Members present may adjourn without further notice. Superintendents and Administrators of Member School Districts are encouraged to participate.

ARTICLE VI - ELECTION OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS. Section 1 requires an odd number of Directors, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9, with the Board having discretion over the number; the Board must consider a change whenever an election produces fewer candidates than open seats and before seeking candidates to fill a vacancy under Section 6; the Secretary communicates any change promptly; a decrease is accomplished by attrition, which may result in an eight member Board for up to one year until the next election, while an increase is accomplished by election, and the Board may call a mid-year special election to increase the number. Section 2 makes any Member eligible, with only one Member from each Member School District serving at a time, and adds that the Intermediate School District pays annual membership dues directly to the Association and is therefore entitled to appoint one (1) Trustee to a 3-year term on the Board of Directors; if the ISD declines, the Board must be notified in writing within 30 days of a Board election so the seat can be filled by election. Section 3 sets three-year terms continuing until a successor is elected and qualified. Section 4 requires the Board to convene an Election Committee by May 1 yearly comprised of the three most recently elected Members of the Board; the committee seeks candidates creating geographical balance throughout Oakland County; Board Candidate Application Forms go to all Member School Districts; completed applications are due before the form's deadline; nominations cannot be made from the floor; election takes place at the June meeting, by written ballot if there are more candidates than vacancies, and by the Section 6 vacancy procedure if fewer. Section 5 allows resignation by written notice and removal by the Members or the Board with cause as defined in Appendix I by affirmative vote of a majority of the Members or Directors then in office, excluding the subject Director. Section 6 sets the vacancy procedure: the Board first considers decreasing the number of Directors, and if it retains the current number the President notifies Members, application forms are sent to each district, and the Board appoints a member at its next meeting to serve until the next scheduled election. Section 7 provides that failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes a resignation, though the Board may grant an excused absence on written request to the President within thirty (30) days of the missed meeting.

ARTICLE VII - BOARD OF DIRECTORS. The Board carries out the purposes in Article II of the Articles of Incorporation. A regular annual Board meeting is held without other notice than the Bylaws, with date and time set by the Board, and additional regular meetings may be set by resolution. Special meetings may be called by the President or any two Directors, who may fix the place. Notice of special meetings is given at least two days by written notice delivered personally, by phone or by email; attendance waives notice except when a Director attends to object to an unlawfully called meeting. A majority constitutes a quorum, and the act of a majority of Directors serving at a meeting with a quorum is the act of the Board. Directors receive no stated salaries but may be allowed a fixed sum and expenses of attendance by resolution. Action may be taken without a meeting by written consent signed by all Directors. Section 9 makes records and business of all Board proceedings confidential absent advance authorization. Section 10 requires the Board to create and maintain Board Operating Procedures used in conjunction with the Bylaws.

ARTICLE VIII - OFFICERS. The Board elects from among current Directors a President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer as soon as practical after the annual appointment of Directors. Terms run until the next annual meeting and until successors are chosen; officers may be removed with cause by majority vote of the Directors and may resign by written notice; the Directors fill vacancies. Officers receive no stated salaries but may be allowed a fixed sum and expenses. The President is Chief Executive Officer, executes authorized conveyances and contracts, and presides at Directors' meetings; the Vice-President acts in the President's absence, and absent both the Directors present designate a presiding officer. The Secretary attends all Board meetings, records all votes and minutes in a book kept for the purpose, gives notice of meetings, and may execute instruments with the President; at the Board's annual discretion the office may be divided into Corresponding Secretary and Recording Secretary. The Treasurer has custody of funds and securities, keeps accounts, deposits monies in designated depositories, disburses funds taking proper vouchers, reports on transactions and financial condition, and if required gives a bond. Section 8 allows the Board to require bonds of all officers, with the Association assuming the cost.

ARTICLE IX - COMMITTEES. The Board may designate standing and ad hoc committees. Committee quorum is twenty-five (25%) percent of appointed representatives, each present representative having one vote; districts may designate alternates who count for quorum and vote only when the primary representative is absent. Section 3 requires each standing and ad hoc committee to elect a Chairperson annually from the appointed representatives, adds that where the elected chair is not a member of the Board of Directors the Association Board shall appoint one of its Directors to serve as Vice-Chair, sets the election as the first order of business at the first meeting after July 1, and requires written notice of the election date, time and place at least seven (7) calendar days in advance. Chairs establish and distribute schedules and agendas, maintain attendance records, distribute minutes, and report to the Board through the President; a chair may resign by written notice to the President and may be removed without cause by majority vote of appointed representatives present or of the Board. Section 4 establishes the Government Relations Committee as a standing committee to receive and share legislative information with Member School Districts, meeting at least 6 times per year; each district should appoint a representative at its annual organizational meeting; a Chairperson is elected annually at the first committee meeting after January 31, each district in attendance casting one vote; in the absence of an elected Vice Chair the Vice President of OCSBA assumes the position, and where the elected chair is not a Board member the Association Board appoints one of its Directors as Vice-Chair. Legislative Priorities are reviewed and revised annually, submitted to the Board for approval, and then provided to the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee and Member School Districts. Section 5 establishes the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee as a standing committee meeting at least once per year, with members appointed annually by the OCSBA President and eligible for reappointment, electing a Chairperson at the first meeting after appointment, and including the Government Relations Committee Chairperson. Resolutions or bylaws revisions may be initiated by a Member School District Board, the Board of Directors, the Government Relations Committee or the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee, must be submitted in writing, and are addressed at the committee's next meeting; approved Legislative Priorities are included in drafted resolutions. The Board reviews all proposals before submission to Member School Districts, which vote at their next meeting within a window of at least forty (40) calendar days with the deadline specified on the ballot or resolution. Resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts become the official position of the Association as interpreted and pursued by its Board of Directors.

ARTICLE X - DISSOLUTION. Assets are distributed as provided in Article VIII of the Articles of Incorporation. No part of net earnings may inure to any Member, Director or Officer, as prohibited by Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or the Michigan General Sales Tax Act or Michigan Use Tax Act.

ARTICLE XI - FIDUCIARY AND FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITIES. Expenditures may not exceed the approved annual budget, and no committee may create financial liability unless authorized by a majority of the Members. Board approval and signatures of both the President and Treasurer are required for any expenditure exceeding $2,500; expenditures up to $2,500 must be approved by either the Board President or the Treasurer; if the President or Treasurer is absent or disabled, the Vice-President may approve. The Treasurer distributes reports to all Board members quarterly or on request; presents a budget for the upcoming fiscal year (July 1 to June 30) no later than the June Board of Directors meeting; presents end of year revenue and expense reports for the immediately preceding fiscal year no later than August 30; and the approved budget and annual report of income and expenditures are presented at the first fall Member Meeting, with accounting records closed annually for IRS filings. Annually the Association performs certain agreed-upon procedures on its financial records, with the year-end report available to the Board before the annual Board and Member meetings; an external audit is conducted in place of agreed-upon procedures only if required by law or a third party. The Board may enter an Administrative and Financial Services Agreement with Oakland Schools, monitored by the Treasurer.

ARTICLE XII - INDEMNIFICATION. Eleven sections indemnify directors and officers to the fullest extent authorized by the Michigan Nonprofit Association Act, for third-party claims (Section 1) and for claims brought by or in the right of the Association (Section 2), covering expenses including attorneys' fees, judgments, penalties, fines and settlement amounts where the Indemnitee acted in good faith. Section 3 bars indemnification for actions brought by the Indemnitee unless authorized by the Board or brought successfully to enforce the Article. Section 4 requires a determination by majority vote of a quorum of Directors not party to the action, by a committee of not less than two (2) disinterested Directors, or by independent legal counsel in a written opinion. Section 5 requires prompt advancement of expenses upon an unlimited general undertaking to repay. Sections 6 through 11 cover partial indemnification, employees and agents, non-exclusivity capped at actual expenses incurred, liability insurance, severability, and definitions of "other enterprises," "fines" and "serving at the request of the Association."

ARTICLES XIII-XVI. The fiscal year is determined by the Board of Directors. Article XIV requires officers, directors, committee members and employees to avoid conflicts; a transaction with an interested director is not void or voidable if it is fair and reasonable when authorized or if material facts are disclosed and it is approved without counting that director's vote; an interested person must give notice and refrain from voting or exerting influence; a conflicted Board member is not counted toward quorum on that matter, and the minutes must reflect the disclosure, the abstention and the quorum situation. Article XV covers contracts and conveyances by Board resolution, execution of instruments, borrowing, adjourned meetings by a majority of Directors present whether or not a quorum, notices by electronic communication to the last known district-provided email address, action by written consent filed with the minutes, remote participation by two-way communication constituting presence in person, and a corporate seal inscribed with the Association name and the words "Corporate Seal" and "Michigan." Article XVI provides that the Bylaws may be altered or amended by vote of the Member School Districts on a written ballot with at least a forty (40) day voting period, one vote per district, while grammatical errors not changing meaning may be corrected by the Board without a membership vote; the Board may adopt additional rules not inconsistent with the Articles of Incorporation or Bylaws unless a local, state or national emergency has been declared, and in a declared emergency may set aside rules regarding meetings, elections and Association affairs.

APPENDIX 1 - DEFINITION OF CAUSE FOR REMOVING A BOARD MEMBER OR OFFICER, adopted by the OCSBA Board of Directors on September 16, 2020. It recites the three primary legal duties of a nonprofit board - duty of care (prudent use of all assets including facility, people and good will), duty of loyalty (advancing the mission, recognizing and disclosing conflicts of interest, deciding in the nonprofit's best interest), and duty of obedience (obeying applicable laws and regulations, following its own bylaws, adhering to stated corporate purposes) - and notes board members also shape culture, strategic focus, effectiveness, financial sustainability, and serve as ambassadors and advocates. Cause for removal includes acts of malfeasance, misfeasance or nonfeasance; willful failure to follow OCSBA bylaws; willful neglect of duties; failure to disclose a conflict of interest or using the Association for personal gain; using the Board position or OCSBA logo in a political endorsement; frequently missed Board or committee meetings; creating an unhealthy or dysfunctional boardroom through inappropriate behavior or disrespect; and ethical concerns such as discrimination, harassment or criminal behaviors. The appendix concludes that removal should occur only when absolutely necessary, with the reasons left to the Association's other Directors and Members.

2026_355_2026_spring_proposed_new_resolu.paragraph: Oakland County School Boards Association ballot material for spring 2026 presenting one proposed new resolution: that OCSBA opposes tying any school funding to waiving the attorney-client privilege. The rationale cites the FY26 school aid budget, in which section 31aa school safety and mental health categorical funding required districts to opt in, with opting-in districts agreeing to cooperate with an investigation, including waiving attorney-client privilege, following a mass-casualty incident. The remainder of the three-page document reprints OCSBA's continuing resolutions for reference, each with its adoption and amendment dates.
2026_355_2026_spring_proposed_new_resolu.page:
**Proposed new resolution**
"OCSBA opposes tying any school funding to waiving the attorney-client privilege."

**Rationale**
In the FY26 school aid budget, section 31aa school safety and mental health categorical funding required districts to "opt in." Any district that opted in to receive 31aa funds agreed to cooperate with an investigation, including waiving the attorney-client privilege, following a mass-casualty incident. The rationale states that while cooperation with investigations after a mass casualty event is necessary to prevent another event, the attorney-client privilege must remain sacred, that the courts have ruled on this issue, and that nothing would stop the legislature from tying waiver of the privilege to other funding in the future.

**Adoption threshold**
Under OCSBA Bylaws Article IX, Section 5, resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) member school districts become the official position of the association as interpreted and pursued by its board of directors.

**Continuing resolutions reprinted for reference**

| Resolution | Dates |
| --- | --- |
| Accountability and Transparency | Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025 |
| Broadband Access and Devices | Adopted 9/11/2021; Amended 6/5/2025 |
| Early Childhood | Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025 |
| Early On Michigan | Adopted 1/26/2026 |
| Evidence-Based Decision Making | Adopted 9/24/2019 |
| Lame Duck | Adopted 9/24/2019 |
| Local Control | Adopted 9/24/2019 |
| Mental Health | Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025 |
| Non-Partisan Elections | Adopted 1/9/2026 |
| School Aid | Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025 |
| School Finance Research Collaborative (SFRC) | Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 9/11/2021, 3/3/2023, 6/5/2025 |
| School Nutrition | Adopted 3/3/2023; Amended 6/5/2025 |
| School Safety | Adopted 3/3/2023 |
| Special Education | Adopted 9/24/2019 |
| Teacher Shortages | Adopted 9/11/2021; Amended 6/5/2025 |
| Unfunded Mandates | Adopted 9/24/2019 |

**Substance of selected continuing positions**
Accountability and transparency standards, including FOIA and the Open Meetings Act, should apply to every school receiving public funding, including local districts, ISDs, Public School Academies and their authorizers and management companies, and colleges and universities. Broadband should be in any federal or state infrastructure plan, with support for device and software purchase programs and dedicated cybersecurity resources. Early childhood positions support new dollars for universal public preschool for four-year-olds and mandatory kindergarten for five-year-olds; Early On Michigan should be fully funded for infants and toddlers birth to age three. School Aid positions call for constitutionally limiting the School Aid Fund to Pre-K to 12th grade public education, opposing vouchers and tax credit programs, additional funding for Special Education, At-Risk and ELL students, protection of the School Aid Fund from state tax policy changes, and enactment of the annual School Aid Budget no later than June 1 so districts can meet the June 30 budget deadline. Special Education seeks full funding of IDEA, noting that federal legislation initially promised 40 percent of the excess cost. The Association also supports the NSBA, MASB, OCSA and COSSBA legislative agendas when aligned with OCSBA legislative priorities.
2026_355_2026_spring_proposed_new_resolu.verbose:
Ballot and reference packet issued by the Oakland County School Boards Association (OCSBA) for member consideration in spring 2026, footered "Proposed NEW Resolution May, 2026" across three pages, and placed before the Troy School District Board of Education for its June 1, 2026 meeting.

PROPOSED NEW RESOLUTION. The single proposed new resolution reads: "OCSBA opposes tying any school funding to waiving the attorney-client privilege."

RATIONALE. In the FY26 school aid budget, section 31aa school safety and mental health categorical funding required districts to "opt in." Any district that opted in to receive 31aa funds agreed to cooperate with an investigation, including waiving the attorney-client privilege, following a mass-casualty incident. The rationale argues that while cooperation with investigations after a mass casualty event is necessary to prevent another event, the attorney-client privilege must remain sacred; that the courts have ruled on this issue; and that in the future there is nothing to stop the legislature from tying waiver of the attorney-client privilege to other funding.

ADOPTION THRESHOLD. The packet quotes OCSBA Bylaws Article IX, Section 5, Resolution Adoption: resolutions that are approved by at least nineteen (19) member school districts shall be the official position of the association as interpreted and pursued by its board of directors. The continuing resolutions that follow have been adopted by member school districts and are provided for reference only, with adoption and amendment dates noted for each.

ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025]. OCSBA supports holding every school that receives public funding to the same accountability and transparency standards, including FOIA requests and the Open Meetings Act, covering local districts, ISDs, Public School Academies (aka Charter Schools), their authorizers and management companies, and all colleges and universities. Cited as MASB Resolution A 6.65 (c), (d), (f).

BROADBAND ACCESS AND DEVICES [OCSBA Adopted 9/11/2021; Amended 6/5/2025]. Broadband should be included in any federal or state infrastructure plan; OCSBA supports additional federal and state funding to expand affordable and reliable broadband access, federal and state programs for the purchase of internet capable devices and software, and dedicated resources for cybersecurity. Cited as MASB Resolution A-10.30, 2021 amendment.

EARLY CHILDHOOD [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025]. Support for additional new dollars to fund universal, public preschool for all four-year-old children, and support for mandatory kindergarten for all five-year-old children. Cited as MASB Resolution A 6.15 (c).

EARLY ON MICHIGAN [OCSBA Adopted 1/26/2026]. Support for full funding of Early On Michigan, an early intervention program for infants and toddlers from birth to age three with disabilities, developmental delays, or who are at risk for delays due to certain health conditions.

EVIDENCE-BASED DECISION MAKING [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. Support for evidence-based education policy that will maximize opportunities for the highest achievement of each student. Cited as MASB Resolution G 11.01.

LAME DUCK [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. Support for lame duck parameters addressing introduction and accelerated passage of legislation after the November election.

LOCAL CONTROL [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. Support local control of community-governed public schools with elected school boards. Cited as MASB Resolutions A 10.10, A 10.55 and A 12.70.

MENTAL HEALTH [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025]. Support for increased mental health services and professionals in schools and, at a minimum, annual inflation adjusted state resources so schools can both educate and keep students and staff safe; help staff identify potential mental health issues; encourage MDE to develop a model policy for staff on identifying mental health issues and appropriate staff response. Cited as MASB Resolutions G 9.01, G 9.05 and G 9.50.

NON-PARTISAN ELECTIONS [OCSBA Adopted 1/9/2026]. Support for non-partisan school board elections.

SCHOOL AID [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025]. Four parts: (A) specify in Michigan's Constitution that the School Aid Fund is only for Pre-K to 12th grade public education and oppose any attempts to create private school vouchers or tax credit programs (MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (a) and A 10.05); (B) support additional funding for Special Education, At-Risk and ELL students (MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (g) and (j); A 10.55); (C) protect the School Aid Fund and local revenues from state tax policy changes (MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (c); A 10.55); and (D) support enacting the annual School Aid Budget no later than June 1 so districts have factual information to meet their constitutional and statutory requirement to approve a budget by June 30 (MASB Resolution A 10.25 (h)).

SCHOOL FINANCE RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE (SFRC) [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 9/11/2021; 3/3/2023; 6/5/2025]. Support for implementation of SFRC recommendations, with higher funded districts held harmless during implementation. Cited as MASB resolution G 11.01 and A-10.25, 2021 amendment.

SCHOOL NUTRITION [OCSBA Adopted 3/3/2023; Amended 6/5/2025]. Support for codification of free universal meals.

SCHOOL SAFETY [OCSBA Adopted 3/3/2023]. Support for adequate state resources allowing schools to both educate and keep students and staff safe.

SPECIAL EDUCATION [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. Support for full funding of the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), noting that federal legislation initially promised to provide 40 percent of the excess cost to educate students with disabilities but that appropriations have fallen short, leaving states and local school districts to make up the difference. Cited as MASB Resolution A 5.01 and NSBA Advocacy: IDEA.

TEACHER SHORTAGES [OCSBA Adopted 9/11/2021; Amended 6/5/2025]. Support for statewide initiatives to address teacher shortages and retain teachers while maintaining quality teacher preparation programs, potentially including incentives to enter and complete a teaching college program, incentives for teachers to remain in the classroom, and easing the process for teachers certified in other states to obtain Michigan certification. Cited as MASB 2021-2022 Legislative Priority.

UNFUNDED MANDATES [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. Opposition to any state or federal legislation that increases costs for school districts without full funding, and encouragement for the Michigan Legislature to oppose federal laws or programs that are not fully funded and thus cost the state valuable resources. Cited as MASB Resolution A 10.20.

ALIGNED AGENDAS [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 6/5/2025]. When aligned with OCSBA legislative priorities, OCSBA also supports the National School Boards Association (NSBA) Legislative Agenda, the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) Legislative Agenda, the Oakland County Superintendents Association (OCSA) Legislative Agenda, and the Consortium of State School Board Associations (COSSBA) Legislative Agenda.

LINKS. MASB Resolutions at https://www.masb.org/resolutions.aspx; NSBA Advocacy: IDEA at https://www.nsba.org/Advocacy; COSSBA Advocacy at https://www.cossba.org/advocacy.

2026_356_2026_spring_proposed_amendments.paragraph: Two-page OCSBA packet setting out proposed 2026 bylaws updates for member district consideration. Amendment 1 would add language to Article VI, Section 2 allowing a member district that pays dues directly to the Association to appoint a Trustee to the Board of Directors, specifically entitling the Intermediate School District, which pays annual dues of currently $6,000 per year, to appoint one Trustee to a 3-year term. Amendment 2 would revise Article IX, Sections 3 and 4 so that when an elected committee chair is not a Board member, the Association Board appoints one of its Directors as Vice-Chair.
2026_356_2026_spring_proposed_amendments.page:
**What it is**
OCSBA document headed "PROPOSED BYLAWS UPDATES FOR 2026," presenting two proposed amendments with rationales and reference copies of related unchanged bylaw language, prepared for member district voting in May 2026.

**Proposed Amendment 1: ISD appointment to the Board of Directors**
Adds language to Article VI, Election of Board of Directors, Section 2 (Eligibility). The existing text keeps the rule that any Member is eligible for election and only one Member from each Member School District may serve at any given time. The added sentences read that the Intermediate School District pays annual membership dues directly to the Association, and is therefore entitled to appoint one (1) Trustee to a 3-year term on the Board of Directors; if the ISD chooses not to exercise that right, the Board of Directors shall be notified in writing within 30 days of a Board election so the seat can be filled by election.

Rationale: like every other member district the ISD is a member of MASB and therefore of the Association, but it is the only member district that also pays annual dues directly to the Association, currently $6,000 per year. The proposal is described as providing board continuity for a working Board where filling all 9 positions is a struggle, and as consistently filling 1 seat, without altering the total number of Directors or the limit of one director per district. It cites the ISD's in-kind donations of event space with AV support (equipment and staff), legislative affairs/advocacy support, and no-cost employee speakers, and notes that ISD dues cover the entire cost the Association pays the ISD for Event Management services (staff, online registration, collection and processing of meeting fees, onsite event support) and Financial Services support (monthly financial accounting, filing annual tax and state reports).

**Reference language, unchanged**
Article III, Section 1 on Members; Article IV on Dues (annual MASB grant to CASBA members, ISD membership dues not to exceed the MASB CASBA grant, contributions and gifts); and Article VI, Section 1 (odd number of Directors, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9).

**Proposed Amendment 2: committee chair or vice-chair on the Board**
Ensures that either the Chair or Vice-Chair of every OCSBA committee is a member of the Board of Directors (BOD), by adding or revising language in two sections of Article IX.

Article IX, Section 3 (Committee Chairs) would add: in the event that the elected committee chair is not a member of the Board of Directors, the Association Board shall appoint one of its Directors to serve as Vice-Chair of the committee. Surrounding provisions are unchanged, including annual election of a Chairperson from appointed representatives as the first order of business at the committee's first meeting after July 1, with written notice not less than seven (7) calendar days before the vote.

Article IX, Section 4 (The Government Relations Committee) keeps annual election of a Chairperson from appointed Members at the first committee meeting after January 31, one vote per Member School District, and the provision that absent an elected Vice Chair the Vice President of OCSBA assumes the position, while adding the same appointment sentence.

Rationale: for Section 3, any member can chair any committee, so assigning a Board member as Vice-Chair provides BOD support, ensures two-way communication with the BOD, and ensures compliance with BOD procedures and bylaws. For Section 4, some Directors never attend Government Relations Committee meetings even though the GRC Vice Chair must attend regularly; both GRC officers need advocacy involvement and attendance at events such as MASB Behind the Scenes and the NSBA Advocacy Institute, so the OCSBA Vice President is not always best suited and the Board should decide which Director serves.
2026_356_2026_spring_proposed_amendments.verbose:
OCSBA packet titled "PROPOSED BYLAWS UPDATES FOR 2026," two pages, setting out two proposed amendments to the bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association for member school district consideration in May 2026, each accompanied by a rationale and, for Amendment 1, reference copies of related bylaw language that would not change. The item appeared on the Troy School District Board of Education agenda for June 1, 2026.

PROPOSED AMENDMENT 1. Headline: a member district that pays dues directly to the Association may appoint a Trustee to a seat on the Board of Directors. The change adds language to ARTICLE VI, ELECTION OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS, Section 2, Eligibility. The section as shown reads that any Member is eligible to be elected to the Association's Board of Directors and that only one Member from each Member School District is allowed to serve on the Board at any given time, followed by the new language: the Intermediate School District pays annual membership dues directly to the Association, and is therefore entitled to appoint one (1) Trustee to a 3-year term on the Board of Directors; if the ISD chooses to not exercise their right to appoint a Director, the Board of Directors shall be notified, in writing, within 30 days of a Board election so that the seat can be filled by election.

RATIONALE FOR AMENDMENT 1. Like every other member district, the ISD is a member of MASB and is therefore a member of the Association. However, to support the Association, the ISD is the only member district that also pays annual dues, currently $6,000 per year, directly to the Association. The proposal is said to help the Association by providing board continuity: the Board of Directors is a working board and it is a struggle to fill all 9 positions, so the proposal will help to consistently fill 1 seat. An appointment by a dues-paying district will not alter the total number of Directors, and the limit of one director per district does not change. Given what the rationale calls the unparalleled financial and in-kind support the ISD provides, an appointed ISD Director is characterized as fair and reasonable. The ISD provides in-kind donations of event space with AV support (equipment and staff) and legislative affairs and advocacy support, and when requested provides employee speakers at no cost to the Association. The ISD's annual dues cover the entire cost that the Association pays to the ISD for service agreements: Event Management services, including but not limited to staff, online registration, collection and processing of meeting fees and onsite event support; and Financial Services support, including but not limited to monthly financial accounting and filing annual tax and state reports.

RELATED LANGUAGE PROVIDED FOR REFERENCE ONLY, WHICH WOULD NOT CHANGE. Article III, Membership, Section 1, Members: the Association is organized upon a membership basis, and any publicly elected Board of Education member of a school district located in Oakland County or any elected Oakland ISD Board of Education member (referred to as "Member School Districts"), that is also a member in good standing in the Michigan Association of School Boards ("MASB"), is an eligible general member of the Association. Article IV, Dues: the Association shall be financed by an annual MASB grant to its County Area School Boards Association (CASBA) members, Intermediate School District membership dues in an amount not to exceed the MASB CASBA grant, and by contributions and gifts accepted by the Association. Article VI, Election of Board of Directors, Section 1, Number of Directors: the Board of Directors shall consist of an odd number of Directors, with no fewer than 7 nor more than 9 members.

PROPOSED AMENDMENT 2. Headline: ensure that either the Chair or Vice-Chair of every OCSBA committee is a member of the Board of Directors (BOD). The change adds or revises language in two sections of ARTICLE IX, COMMITTEES.

Article IX, Section 3, Committee Chairs, as amended: each standing and ad hoc committee shall elect a Chairperson annually from the appointed representatives; in the event that the elected committee chair is not a member of the Board of Directors, the Association Board shall appoint one of its Directors to serve as Vice-Chair of the committee; the election shall be the first order of business at the committee's first meeting after July 1st, unless otherwise specified in the Bylaws; and written notice of the election date, time and place shall be provided to all appointed representatives not less than seven (7) calendar days prior to the meeting at which the vote will occur.

Rationale for adding this language to Section 3: any member can be elected to chair any committee, meaning the chair does not have to be a member of the Board of Directors. When a committee chair is not a BOD member, assigning a BOD member as Vice-Chair will provide BOD support for the committee, ensure direct two-way communication between the committee and the BOD, and ensure compliance with BOD procedures and Association bylaws.

Article IX, Section 4, The Government Relations Committee, Committee Membership/Leadership, as revised: a Committee Chairperson will be elected annually from the appointed Members at the first committee meeting after January 31st, with each Member School District in attendance having one (1) vote cast by its appointed representative; in the absence of an elected Vice Chair, the Vice President of OCSBA will assume the position of Vice Chair; and in the event that the elected committee chair is not a member of the Board of Directors, the Association Board shall appoint one of its Directors to serve as Vice-Chair of the committee.

Rationale for revising the current language in Section 4: while all Directors serve on one or more committees, Directors are not necessarily involved in the Government Relations Committee, and some Directors never attend GRC meetings even though the Vice Chair of the GRC must regularly attend them. Like the GRC Chair, the Vice Chair needs to be knowledgeable and actively involved in advocacy, and both the Chair and Vice Chair of the GRC need to provide leadership for members by regularly attending state and national advocacy conferences and events, such as MASB Behind the Scenes and the NSBA Advocacy Institute. For these reasons the OCSBA Vice President is not always the person best suited to fulfill the role of GRC Vice Chair, and the OCSBA Board of Directors should be allowed to decide which of its Directors is best suited to serve in the role.
